answer: Each identity registers one nebula mirror array and locks an 80-credit key-bound bond. Each epoch it files a mirror star count plus the nebula field brightness reading. A falcon auditor recomputes the count from the nebula brightness table and mirror area, allowing 5% tolerance; a mismatch burns the bond. Audit fees grow down the queue: the kth mirror pays 18+4(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes pay 80,000 in bonds plus 2,016,000 in fees. A rented-mirror ring fails because a rented mirror count carries the owner's key, not the tenant's. One honest mirror pays 80 once plus 18 and keeps full weight.
